gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-satoshi: Refined and bookish, Noto Serif Hentaigana stands tall, its thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones. Satoshi is the plain sans answer to that, every stroke cut to one width, and that steadiness is the pair's best quality.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-switzer: Switzer reads like wire: tubular, tall-waisted, every stroke one thickness. Noto Serif Hentaigana above it thins its bowls gracefully, so the page moves between a drawn skeleton and softer, tapering letters.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana-work-sans: Work Sans reads as drawn with one pen tip, modern and level. Noto Serif Hentaigana brings a modest thick and thin rhythm and a towering lowercase, and that gentle friction is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-archivo: Archivo brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, with an editorial ease. And Noto Serif Kannada, traditional and literary, adds slight but visible thick-thin variation that the plain sans below it never attempts.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-fs-asap: Noto Serif Kannada is traditional and literary, with softly thinner curves on top. Its strength is that gentle modulation, while Asap counters with a body height nearly matching its capitals and open, arc-like forms.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-fs-epilogue: Curvy, wire-thin, a bit unbuttoned. Noto Serif Kannada keeps its stroke modulation tempered up top, while Epilogue's same-width strokes frame each counter below, so the sans-serif reads as the looser of the two.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-fs-fira-sans: Noto Serif Kannada varies its strokes softly, in a traditional, literary way. Fira Sans moves its stems and arcs in lockstep with a larger-than-usual x-height, and that steady sans against the gentle swell is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-fs-public-sans: Traditional, literary heading, hefty body. Public Sans starts the second half with broad open counters and a lowercase that looks heavy, and a slightly larger size for Noto Serif Kannada would let its measured swell hold up.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-fs-supreme: Slightly lighter joins and terminals give Noto Serif Kannada its mild but visible contrast, with an enlarged lowercase. Supreme, a crisp sans, holds its letters open in a thick, heavy-looking band, and that weight is the standout.
gen-gf-noto-serif-kannada-general-sans: Traditional and literary, Noto Serif Kannada draws its crossbars a bit finer than its main stems. And General Sans holds a compass-pencil consistency with an x-height filling the line, so a slightly larger heading size would suit it.
